newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Orrefors Kosta Boda sees 1996 profits crash.
newsitem.headline: Orrefors Kosta Boda sees 1996 profits crash.

text.p: Swedish luxury glassmaker Orrefors Kosta Boda posted a 43 percent plunge in its 1996 profit after financial items on Thursday.

The glass maker, that was taken over by a Swedish/Danish consortium late last year, said sales for the year fell six percent to 664 million crowns while profit after financial items crashed 43 percent to 37.1 million crowns.
"After very weak sales at the start of the year, a recovery was noted in the second and third quarters," Orrefors Kosta Boda said in a statement.
"But this positive development ended in the year's last months."
It said sales were particularly badly affected in the Swedish and Western European markets.
"The reason in Sweden is a combination of imported low priced goods and low private consumption," it said.

Orrefors Kosta Boda said it was continuing to pursue a coooperation agreement with Denmark's luxury goods maker Royal Copenhagen ROYCb.ST to combine distribution and sales efforts in some export markets.

Orrefors Kosta Boda was delisted from the Stockholm bourse in December after being taken over by a consortium of Scandinavian Equity Partners, Royal Copenhagen, and Swedish investment group Proventus.
